body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.
_Last reviewed 2026-02-09._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-accounting-discrepancy-intake-and-triage.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)", "status": "published", "date": "2025-04-22", "text": "## Definition (use this phrase)
We classify a case as a *token accounting discrepancy* when a customer claims that billed token totals (Console Usage and/or invoice export) do not match their own calculation from application logs or local tokenization.
## Approved intake channels
We track where the report first arrived, because it affects response time and deduplication.
- Jira (customer-support): SUP-* ticket created directly by Support
- Slack: #support threads (often started from Intercom/Zendesk summaries)
- Gmail: finance/billing or CSM forwards to leadership/finance"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-accounting-discrepancy-intake-and-triage.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)", "status": "published", "date": "2025-04-22", "text": "## How to avoid double counting
1. If a report arrives in Slack or Gmail, file a SUP ticket and link it.
2. Mark the SUP ticket label `token-accounting` and add the origin channel in the description (Slack/Gmail).
3. In weekly reporting, count the case by *origin* (Slack vs Gmail vs Jira), not by total artifacts.
## Common root causes to check
- Streaming retries/reconnect (tokens can be emitted twice)
- Client counts only final chunk tokens
- Different tokenizer / unicode normalization
- Whitespace/newlines included in input strings
- Tool-call serialization adds tokens
- Prefix-cache billing bug (rare; see SUP-3009)"}, {"source": "sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-556901-cache-hit-invoice-line-explanation-and-provisional-credit.json", "chunk": "3/7", "kind": "Jira ticket", "title": "SUP-556901: Invoice shows separate 'cache-hit tokens' line plus 'generated tokens' for same time window — clarification and potential adjustment requested", "status": "In Progress", "date": "2026-03-03", "text": "  - 2) Run a 3-day batch of repeated prompt variants that should hit the cache ~65% of the time, and record tokens generated vs. returned from cache in the runtime metrics console.
  - 3) Download billing invoice CSV for the same window and inspect lines for that API key. Note presence of both 'generated' and 'cache-hit' lines with overlapping timestamps.
  - 4) Compare runtime token counters (runtime/tracing) to invoice meter rows for token counts and prices per token.
  - 5) Share artifacts: runtime metrics links, raw CSV, and the invoice PDF.
observed_behavior: Invoice shows two line items for the same hour ranges: one with 1,245,320 generated tokens and a second labeled 'cache-hit tokens' with 812,450 tokens. The customer sees in the runtime console that ~810k tokens were served from KV cache and expected these to be excluded from billable generated token usage or be discounted under their dedicated contract. The invoice's unit price for 'cache-hit tokens' matches the standard per-token generation price, producing a ~40% higher charge than expected."}, {"source": "sources/linear/engineering/ENG-21456-rate-limit-refund-allocation-export-fix.json", "chunk": "5/6", "kind": "Linear issue", "title": "Resolve invoice rounding + rate-limit refund allocation causing NetSuite export variance", "status": "In Progress", "date": "2025-03-05", "text": "  - 2025-03-05 - LO: Canary run queued; monitoring dashboard prepared. Waiting on Ops to approve S3 backfill bucket lifecycle change.
sql_queries:
  - -- Repro query: invoices where exported_total != computed_total
SELECT invoice_id, exported_total, SUM(line_amount) as computed_total, exported_total - SUM(line_amount) as diff_cents
FROM billing.invoice_lines l JOIN billing.exports e ON l.invoice_id = e.invoice_id
WHERE e.export_date >= '2025-01-01'
GROUP BY invoice_id, exported_total
HAVING ABS(exported_total - SUM(line_amount)) > 0.01;
  - -- Identify fractional credit patterns
SELECT invoice_id, COUNT(*) as credit_lines, SUM(line_amount) as credit_total
FROM billing.invoice_lines
WHERE credit_type = 'rate_limit_refund'
GROUP BY invoice_id
HAVING SUM(line_amount) != ROUND(SUM(line_amount), 2);"}, {"source": "sources/jira/misc-requests/INT-4928-expose-invoice-metadata-console.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Jira ticket", "title": "INT-4928: Expose invoice/billing metadata in admin console for finance ops", "status": "In Progress", "date": "2025-11-18", "text": "Steps to reproduce/workaround: 1) Finance requests invoice detail for a customer; 2) Support opens internal billing report spreadsheet or asks engineering to run query; 3) Export attached CSV and share.
Logs / data: Not applicable for bug reproduction.
Proposed solution: Add a restricted "Invoices" view in the admin console behind the finance role flag that surfaces: invoice_id, customer_account_id, billing_period_start/end, gross_amount, credits_applied, issuing_region, linked_subscription_ids, download PDF link, and reference to the original charge_id. Implement RBAC check (finance/admin) and paginate results. Start with a read-only view; no edits.
Acceptance criteria: - Finance role can view invoice list and click into invoice details for rows in the last 24 months. - Download link points to pre-signed PDF stored in internal S3. - Audit log entries recorded for invoice view events. - Feature behind feature-flag for safe rollout."}, {"source": "sources/slack/support/1745126789-weekly-export-partial-day-aggregation-mismatch.json", "chunk": "4/4", "kind": "Slack thread", "title": "#support thread 1745126789-weekly-export-partial-day-aggregation-mismatch", "status": "n/a", "date": "2025-04-20", "text": "(continued) # sample tail
eve-customer: Downloaded and checked — the new CSV shows 2025-02-28 and 2025-03-01 rows with tokens: 2025-02-28 total_tokens 21,300; 2025-03-01 total_tokens 14,120. Dashboard and CSV now match.
carla-billing: Based on the +35,420 tokens, that's $0.00xx; invoice INV-2025-0315 variance is $312 because earlier CSV had omitted some higher-cost calls (model tiered). We'll issue a credit note CN-2025-0318 for $312 and adjust the monthly usage summary. I'll DM the customer with details.
eve-customer: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Can you also confirm whether this could happen again around month boundaries?
david-telemetry: We've deployed lock-order fix and added an alert for >5% missing tokens in a daily export window. Also improved backfill retry for DB lock errors. Should be much less likely.
ben-support: Closing loop: we've re-run the backfill, re-exported CSV, billing will issue credit, and we deployed a fix. Please reopen if you see any more discrepancies. :thumbsup:
eve-customer: All good on our end, thanks everyone! :rocket:"}]}
